request.spec: Reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner. Respond with 409.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner. Respond with 409.

agent.result_text:
The full suite is green: **259 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**.

## Summary

The change enforces telephone uniqueness across all owners when creating one via `POST /api/owners`, responding **409 Conflict** on a duplicate.

The endpoint pipeline (`owners.POST.yml`) already ran a `EnsureOwnerUnique` step and threw `DuplicateOwnerException`, handled globally as 409. Only the rule inside that step needed to broaden:

- **`EnsureOwnerUnique.java`** — was rejecting only when *both* last name **and** telephone matched (checked against `findByLastName`). Now it iterates `findAll()` and rejects if **any** other owner shares the telephone (skipping self by id, harmless for a new owner). This broader rule subsumes the earlier checkpoints — an identical owner (cp01) and a same-last-name-and-telephone owner (cp02) still get rejected because their telephone collides.
- **`DuplicateOwnerException.java`** — updated the javadoc to describe the telephone-uniqueness rule.

The new `Cp03Tests` (telephone unique across all owners) passes, and the earlier `Cp01Tests`/`Cp02Tests` and `OwnerRestControllerV1Tests` remain green — including the allow-case where two owners share a last name but have distinct telephones.
